event_title: Oyebanji declared winner of governorship election
description: The governorship election was held on 20 June 2026. At about 3:13 a.m. on Sunday 21 June, INEC's State Returning Officer, Prof. Adenike Oladiji, declared Biodun Oyebanji (APC) the winner with 319,224 votes, against 40,543 for Wole Oluyede (PDP) and 12,872 for Dare Bejide (ADC). The announced totals were 384,940 accredited voters, 375,777 valid votes, 6,332 rejected votes and 382,109 votes cast.
source: Channels TV: INEC declares APC's Oyebanji winner of Ekiti governorship election (updated, 21 Jun 2026)
claim_source_map: Declaration, time, Returning Officer and all totals: Channels TV, Vanguard and Daily Trust. Full party table: ThisDay live updates and a Channels Television results graphic (data source INEC). Check: the 15 party totals in that table add up to 375,777 only if the PDP total is 40,543, and valid plus rejected votes equal the 382,109 votes cast.
unconfirmed_details: INEC's own declaration document (Form EC8E or INEC's declaration post) has not been read, so the result stays marked as awaiting a primary record even though the reporting is consistent. The PDP total is printed as 40,533 by The Whistler and Premium Times; the arithmetic above shows 40,543 is the consistent figure, so 40,533 is almost certainly a typographical error. Other slips: Vanguard labels the ADC candidate ADP, TVC News gives 375,778 valid votes, and one Premium Times item prints the ADC total as 2,872. The reported win in all 16 LGAs (Premium Times, allAfrica) is not in the description; INEC's LGA table has not been read.
claims_and_disputes: Reported claims, not findings: the ADC candidate alleged irregularities and Oyebanji rejected the claim (Channels TV); observers' concerns about vote-buying and intimidation were reported by Legit.ng and Dataphyte; Yiaga Africa's observation mission raised concerns about the consistency of materials INEC deployed after late candidate-list changes (Channels TV). A pre-election challenge to his APC nomination was dismissed by the Supreme Court (Legit.ng, 24 Jul 2026). Characterisation by media: Premium Times (22 Jun 2026) calls him the first Ekiti governor to secure consecutive re-election, and allAfrica (22 Jun 2026) says he is the first governor re-elected back to back since the state's creation; Dataphyte (19 Jun 2026) notes that no incumbent had won a second consecutive term. Before the vote, Legit.ng and allAfrica (19 Jun) said no incumbent had won re-election since the 1999 return to elected government and that Adebayo, the first governor, served a single term. Premium Times adds that Fayose and Fayemi each served two non-consecutive terms. None of this is an INEC statement.
notes_limitations: Media characterisations are attributed, not adopted. Our own tenure list raises no contradiction, but that is a sanity check, not a source. Registered-voter figures differ: 988,251 in the results graphic and The Whistler, against about 1.06 million in pre-election reports (Dataphyte); not used.
